title: Preemptive slot scheduler with tenant credit awareness and cache affinity
creator: Marcus Cheng
description:
Goal: Build a scheduler that preemptively assigns short-lived inference slots with explicit awareness of tenant credits, SLA band, and KV-cache affinity to reduce cold-start token cost and minimize visible latency regressions during cross-tier spillover. This feature sits in the routing layer and complements the existing admission controller: instead of purely reactive demotion, we hold a small preemptive escrow of slots for enterprise lanes and a cache-affinity bias for warm requests.

Background: Current quota-aware routing reacts when a tenant exhausts credits by immediately demoting traffic to fallback models or regional spillovers. That reactive approach causes sudden latency and quality shifts for paid customers and thundering-cache misses for requests that could have benefited from warm KV cache. We need a gentler, proactive policy which: (1) reduces cache churn, (2) gives enterprise lanes brief preemptive slot guarantees, and (3) enables controlled soft-preemption for free/paid lanes to avoid large-scale SLA violations.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can escrow and release slots per service-class (free/paid/enterprise) with configurable windows (default 10s).
Observed p99 token-latency for enterprise customers does not regress >5% under simulated quota pressure compared to baseline without scheduler.
Cache-affinity score introduced; requests with score >0.75 are prioritized for warm-slot assignment resulting in >=20% fewer cache-miss cold starts in load tests.
When paid tier credits are exhausted, degradation follows soft-preemption windows (configurable) that attenuate rate of demotion and emit rollout metrics to Console.
No user-visible authentication changes; audit logs include slot escrow events for Private deployments.
design_notes: Introduce a Slot Escrow token per tenant that represents a short-lived hold on GPU queue capacity. Escrow tokens decay on use or after window expiration.
Compute a per-request cache_affinity score: weighted( kv_cache_hit_likelihood, recent_model_variant_hits, regional_node_locality ).
Priority ordering: enterprise-escrow > paid-affinity-high > paid-default > free-affinity-high > free-default. Within same priority, use token-age and randomized jitter for fairness.

Soft-preemption: instead of hard kick to fallback model, progressively reduce quality (e.g., quantized variant) for a small fraction of requests during the preemption window, measured by rollout metrics.
Expose tuning knobs via Console: escrow_window_ms, affinity_threshold, preemption_fraction, enterprise_reserve_ratio.
technical_spec: Scheduler component lives in routing-service: new module 'slot-sheriff' to run admission decisions before admission-controller to allocate escrows.

Data model: extend Tenant metadata with {escrow_tokens:int, last_escrow_ts:iso8601, reserve_ratio:float, sla_band:string}. Stored in fast cache (Redis) with consistency shard keys aligned to tenant_id.
API: routing-service GET /route/score returns {priority_score,float, cache_affinity,float, recommended_slot:int}.

Algorithm (high level):
1) compute cache_affinity in 2-3ms using local KV statistics and recent-hit window.
2) if tenant.sla_band == enterprise and tenant.credits > enterprise_min, try allocate escrow up to reserve_ratio.
3) if credits nearing zero, compute preemption_plan which maps N% of requests to lower-cost model variants with exponential backoff.
4) emit decision traces for Console with delta metrics for cost and latency.
Fallback: if Redis shard unavailable, use conservative mode (no new escrows, existing escrows allowed to expire) to avoid overcommit.
Instrumentation: add prom counters for escrow_allocations, escrow_expires, cache_affinity_hits, preemption_invocations, and per-tenant metric tags.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (canary): Enable on internal-tenants namespace with 5% rollouts to verify behavior and metrics instrumentation.
Stage 1 (beta): Enable for paid customers in us-west region, telemetry-only for free-tier to monitor false positives. Duration 2 weeks.
Stage 2 (gradual): Expand to all paid and enterprise across regions with enterprise_reserve_ratio default 0.05; run A/B comparing p99 latencies and cost delta.
Rollback: if enterprise p99 > baseline +5% for consecutive 30m, automatically roll back to reactive-only admission via feature-flag.
testing_plan: Unit tests for escrow lifecycle, eviction, and race windows.
Integration test: multi-tenant simulator that drives credit exhaustion scenarios and measures demotion rates and cache miss ratios.
Load test: synthetic workload replay (based on production traces) with and without scheduler to compare token cost, p95/p99 latency, and cache hit rate.
Chaos test: Redis shard downtime simulation to validate conservative fallback path.
Security test: verify no escalation of privileges or cross-tenant leaks when escrows are allocated or released.
migration_steps: Add Tenant escrow fields with default values; lazy backfill for tenants on first request to avoid large migration lock.
Seed enterprise reserve ratios from existing billing/tier metadata.
Run historical-simulation job to estimate expected escrow churn and cost delta before enabling on a per-customer basis.
risks: Over-reserving slots could reduce overall throughput if reserve_ratio is too high — mitigated by conservative defaults and telemetry-based auto-tune.
Inaccurate cache_affinity scoring may bias against bursty free-tier traffic causing perceived unfairness — mitigated by retrainable heuristic and canary metrics.
Redis availability creates single point for escrow state; conservative fallback reduces behavioral impact but may reduce enterprise guarantees. Consider HA replication.
comments: 2026-03-03 Marcus Cheng: Initial draft posted. Added high-level acceptance criteria. Requested feedback from SRE and Billing on reserve_ratio implications.

2026-03-05 Evelyn Ross: Prototype stub implemented in routing-service. Preliminary local tests show 12% fewer cold-cache tokens under synthetic warm-up workload. Pushed branch feat/slot-scheduler. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/2147

2026-03-07 Omar Farouk: SRE concern - Redis shard key hotness for high-volume tenants. Suggested moving escrow counters into local per-node in-memory with async reconciliation to Redis. Added as follow-up task ENG-42902.

2026-03-09 Priya Nair: Billing review — enterprise_reserve_ratio default of 0.05 seems fine but want telemetry to surface cost delta per-customer before enabling billing changes. Will coordinate with growth team.

2026-03-12 Evelyn Ross: Updated spec to include conservative fail-open behavior when Redis unavailable. Integration tests added to verify fallback path. Scheduling additional load test week of 2026-03-16.
